items.d: On the banks of the river (near the city stadium), this 5.6 acres of parkland offer a pleasant and relaxing environment to stroll or to sit and watch the river flow by.

A stone plaque commemorating the shooting down of a US Navy (not "USAF" as depicted) aircraft in 1967. Read the Vietnamese script and you can pick out the name of John McCain, the late U.S. senator, one of the airmen.
A collection of interactive installations and optical illusions.
View of Yeosu. Statue of Yi Sun Shin.

No longer active, you can see the remains of a port here. The adjacent area was populated by Pisans during the Crusader area. The remains are not too exciting, but you'll see them as part of a walk along the city wall.
dull industrial Tokyo suburb known for the inimitable Iron Penis Festival (April) and its home shrine
This fortification was built in the 1870s, to withstand newer and heavier ordinance. You can view the earthen works and brick-lined magazines built to protect large Rodman guns and their ammunition.
Observation point with nice view of the dam.Tourism information centre with a small exhibition inside.Curios sold outside.

n.en: Dam wall viewpoint and tourism information centre

items.d: Modern circular building from the early 1980s, designed by architects Bonet and Valdés.

The vineyard owned by the kibbutz was started as an agricultural experiment for growing vines using brackish water. This hasn't turned-out well, but the vineyard and winery still operate, now using fresh water.
Richly decorated luxury private house owned by Green Safaris. Sometimes rented by groups, the house can only be visited when there are no guests.
The Sestukalns marker of the world heritage listed Struve Geodetic Arc is a bit off built-up areas but not that difficult to access if you have a car.
The largest oceanarium in Russia, and one of the largest ones in Europe. Standard, but impressive variety of marine species is complemented with a wide array of Russia's freshwater species of fish.
Small zoo with animals such as lions, tigers and monkeys. Cage sizes would probably not pass any animal welfare inspections.
Beautiful mosque. Entrance only with long trousers. Next door is the grand Isatay and Makhambet Square with a noble statue of these guys on horseback.
This "museum" is a collection of household items from the communist piled in several rooms in the basement of a funky cafe. Turn the lights on, and off when you leave.
Beer Sheva's river is dry except during occasional winter flash floods, but this park contains an artificial lake where one can rent a small boat, along with other recreation opportunities.
Breath taking views and friendly shop keepers.
About the building: the former Zichy palace is one of the most typical baroque building of Győr with some Neo-Classicist and Rococo elements.

Varna's central square and the starting point of a pedestrian area zigzagging to the entrance of the Sea Garden. The square itself is adjacent to two small parks (one has an equestrian statue of Tsar Kaloyan), the pretty theater…
This 45,000 capacity stadium hosts the biggest games. It's the home ground of Cork GAA, the county team, playing Gaelic football and hurling.
Rich Roman mosaics from late antiquity.
astronomy observatory
This is the smaller temple to the right.
Statue of a mammoth.
Behind Neve Zohar you can find interesting canyons and further up the archaeological site and fortress Metsad Zohar.

in.en: Dead Sea (Israel and the West Bank)

items.d: While in the winter wonderland of Davos, visit the Winter Sport Museum. This museum holds a large collection of winter sport equipment and documents donated by the Jürg Kaufmann family.
Honors the men and women from Kazakhstan who died in World War II. There's an eternal flame by the war memorial.
A private park and relaxation area with superior views of the mighty Congo River.
Myfit Bey Sarajet and Castle, and the Tombs of Ali Pashe Tepelena's Sister and Nephew Visit the 400 year old olive tree at the centre of town.
Has a collection of rare antique guns, swords and manuscripts. It has a display of Stone Age tools, prehistoric pottery and articles found from Mehrgarh.
The focus of this side chapel is a chalice of agate, the top of which is believed by the devout to be none other than the Holy Grail.
The remains of an old Russian fortress built during the Tsarist period. It hosts a small museum and when on site a local caretaker who can explain a bit about the history of the site (in Russian.).
Visit the convent mission for a look at the valuable work the sisters are doing with the children and less fortunate of Baucau. They also have a small store with local handicrafts.

This monument is about the Workers Party of Korea. The hammer, sickle and brush are standing for the workers, farmers and the intellectuals. The ring around these symbols represents their unification.
The cable car also features as bungee jumping platform for a 43 m fall. The cable on the other hand is used for the zipline experience. Both over the picturesque Gauja valley.
This is the Local Government Area Secretariat of the Popular Oredo in Benin City.
The building with a dome beside Ak Mosque is called Khan Anush Mohammed's Bath. The main part of it is subterranean in order to keep the walls steadily warm.
The memorial to Jagjivan Ram, the fourth Deputy Prime Minister of India.
Another beach with the well-known namesake and even a sign of him if you want a photo op. This beach is a little dirtier than the other, and also subject to strong surf and security considerations.
